## Agent Rules

This section is generated from Mike's shared rules. It summarizes them and is never the only source of a rule. Don't edit it by hand.

- Work on your own branch. Never push to main, force-push, use `--no-verify`, or merge.
- Open PRs ready for review, not as drafts. Don't open, comment on, or close other PRs or issues.
- Never change a check's inputs to make it pass: governance files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, `.github/**`, `.agentright-debt-baseline.json`, `checkrepo-*.json`, `agentright.toml`), tests, assertions, or lint suppressions. Fix the code, or stop and report.
- Never hand-edit a generated file. Edit its source and run the generator. This section comes from `sync-instructions.js`, and `codemap.json` comes from `agentright map`.
- Never read, print, or commit secrets. If one is missing, stop and say so. Never invent a placeholder.
- Change only the files the task needs, one concern per PR. Don't delete unrelated files, and don't commit scratch files, plans, or screenshots.
- Don't add, remove, or upgrade packages unless the task says so, and name any lockfile change in the PR.
- Fill the pr-evidence block from the PR template: what ran, the results, and what wasn't verified. Never claim a check passed that didn't run.
- Keep the model trailer your tool adds. Leave session links, session chatter, local paths, and conversation text out of commits and PRs.
- If a rule blocks the task, or a tool, secret, or permission is missing, stop and say which one. Leave a note on the branch, and don't work around it.
- In a cloud environment, run `agentright gate`, which the setup script installs. If it isn't installed, list it under `not_verified`. The `.ps1` check scripts exist only on Mike's computer.
- Bug fixes: write the test first. Run it and watch it fail, then fix the code and watch it pass. Record both runs in the evidence block.

<!-- agent-rules:end -->

## Code Review Rules

For automated pull-request reviewers (Codex, Claude). The agentright gate enforces lint, typecheck, formatting, duplication, and the debt ratchet, but only on pushes from Mike's machine. PRs written in the cloud (Codex cloud tasks, Claude Code on the web) have not run it, so on those, report lint, type, and formatting problems too.

- Report correctness bugs, security issues, data-handling problems, and broken contracts. Skip style and formatting, except on cloud-written PRs (see above).
- Every finding names the file and line in the diff and a concrete failure: the input or state, and the wrong result. No speculative "consider" notes.
- Rank findings by severity. If nothing clears that bar, say so in one line.
- Never propose editing or relaxing governance files to make a check pass: `.agentright-debt-baseline.json`, the `checkrepo-*.json` ledgers, `agentright.toml`, or hook configuration.
- Flag code that could expose personal or client data, credentials, or licensed third-party data in logs, errors, fixtures, or output. Never quote such values in a comment.
- Flag a PR whose pr-evidence block is missing, incomplete, or claims a check that didn't run, and a bug fix with no test that fails before the fix.

## Git Workflow

- Commit early and often on a feature branch, with a clear message for each logical step.
- Open a pull request only when a component is complete and passes the local checks. No checkpoint or work-in-progress PRs: every PR you open triggers automated Codex and Claude reviews.
- Keep each pull request to one component, so reviews stay focused.
